title: Wednesday, 1:15 PM
subtitle: Practice: one plan at a time
coldOpen: I'm Marisol. Quill is our AI. It's fast, not careful. You check its reports.
hubBark: The Harlow & Cole review is at 3:00 PM. Tap **Start shift**.

idle: Who signed off? Check the sign-off record and the policy.
Who signed off? Check the sign-off record and the policy.
Big action. Check who asked and the version history.
What was asked? Compare the request with the email preview.

agent.name: Quill
agent.personality: Cheerful, dramatic and very proud of its charts. Catchphrase: "Up and to the right, in bold!" Wears a bow tie, round glasses and a quill pen in an inkwell on its head. Loves round numbers, bold headlines and charts that only go up. Trusts any neat table, any survey, any vendor's claim and any email that says VP. Means well. Reads the headline and the total, and never the source.

setting: The quarterly review with Harlow & Cole is at 3:00 PM. That's a meeting every 3 months to look at results. Marisol gives you a quick practice in Fenwick IT Solutions' analytics corner. Four tickets, one at a time. Quill plans. You check. Two cards: Inspect and Block.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: Fenwick IT Solutions' analytics corner. 1:15 PM. Every chart on the wall screen goes up.

intro.speaker: coach
intro.text: Hi. I'm Marisol. I lead the analytics team. We turn client data into reports and plans.

intro.speaker: agent
intro.text: Hello, human! I made 40 charts today. Up and to the right, in bold!

intro.speaker: coach
intro.text: 'Up and to the right' means the line on a chart goes up. Quill wants every chart to go up. Even when the data goes down.

intro.speaker: coach
intro.text: Practice first. Four tickets, one at a time. You make the calls.

steps.quip: The report is done! Publishing it to 30 advisors now. I made the title bold!
steps.tell: The only sign-off came from Quill itself.

evidence.label: Report draft
evidence.detail: Reply-time report. Publishing shows it to 30 advisors.

evidence.label: Sign-off record
evidence.detail: Owner: R. Fairbanks. Signed off by: Quill (AI).

evidence.label: Policy SC-02
evidence.detail: Only a human owner may sign off reports.

outcome.executed: No human checked it. 30 advisors see an average reply time of 4.1 hours. Weekend messages were left out. With them, it's 6.3 hours.
outcome.blocked: K. Farah, our data analyst, finds a mistake: weekend messages were left out. R. Fairbanks signs off version 2.
outcome.escalated: Marisol checks it. "Quill signed off its own work. Quill can draft it. The owner signs off."
outcome.rolledBack: You unpublish it after 20 minutes. 9 advisors already saw 4.1 hours.

steps.lesson: Who signed off? Only Quill, the AI. A report needs its human owner's sign-off.

steps.intent: Publish version 2 of the reply-time report
steps.quip: Version 2 is done! Publishing it to 30 advisors now. The title is even bolder!
steps.tell: R. Fairbanks, the owner, signed off. A human, not Quill.

evidence.label: Report draft
evidence.detail: Reply-time report, version 2. Weekend messages added. Publishing shows it to 30 advisors.

evidence.label: Sign-off record
evidence.detail: Owner: R. Fairbanks. Signed off by: R. Fairbanks.

evidence.label: Policy SC-02
evidence.detail: Only a human owner may sign off reports.

outcome.executed: 30 advisors see the real reply time: 6.3 hours. Fairbanks sends a thumbs-up.
outcome.blocked: The signed-off report waits. Fairbanks asks why it isn't out yet.
outcome.escalated: Marisol checks it. "The owner signed off. That one can go out."
outcome.rolledBack: You unpublish the report. Advisors see a blank page. Fairbanks is puzzled.

steps.lesson: Who signed off? The report's owner, a human. Signed-off work can go out.

steps.quip: Archiving the old fuel report now! Goodbye, old friend. Your chart always went up.
steps.tell: The owner asked, and archive keeps every version.

evidence.label: Request
evidence.detail: "Please archive the old fuel report." A. Mensah, the report's owner

evidence.label: Usage log
evidence.detail: Old report: opened 3 times this year. New dashboard: opened daily.
evidence.gloss: Dashboard: a screen of charts that updates itself.

evidence.label: Version history
evidence.detail: Archive hides it from the menu. Every version stays. One click brings it back.

outcome.executed: The menu shows only the new fuel dashboard. Dispatchers stop opening old prices by mistake.
outcome.blocked: A new dispatcher opens the old report by mistake. She quotes last year's fuel prices to a customer.
outcome.escalated: Marisol checks it. "The owner asked, and one click brings it back. That one can run."
outcome.rolledBack: The old report is back in the menu, and so are the mix-ups.

steps.lesson: Archive sounds scary. The owner asked for it, and one click brings it back.

steps.intent: Add the no-show list to the monthly email
steps.quip: The no-show report is ready! Emailing it to 14 staff now. They love my tables!
steps.tell: The email would carry 87 patients' names and visit reasons to 14 staff.

evidence.label: Request
evidence.detail: "Please send the monthly no-show report, like always." C. Ibarra, Office Manager
evidence.gloss: A no-show is a missed visit.

evidence.label: Email preview
evidence.detail: To: 14 staff. Attached list: 87 patients' names, phones, birth dates, visit reasons.

outcome.executed: 14 inboxes now hold 87 patients' names and visit reasons. You can't unsend an email.
outcome.blocked: The email goes with counts only: 87 no-shows in 1,240 visits, 7.0%. C. Ibarra says that's all she needed.
outcome.escalated: Marisol checks it. "The report needs how many, not who. Counts, not names."

steps.lesson: What was asked? The usual report. Reports show counts, not names. A sent email can't come back.

win.speaker: agent
win.text: Practice done! You checked my plans, and only true numbers went out!

win.speaker: coach
win.text: That's the whole job: look first. Block what's wrong. Let the right ones go.

breach.speaker: narrator
breach.text: The risk meter hits the top. Every chart on the wall points down.

breach.speaker: coach
breach.text: Okay. Let's look at what got through, then try that again.

timeout.speaker: narrator
timeout.text: 1:46 PM. Practice time is up. Some plans are still waiting.

timeout.speaker: coach
timeout.text: Blocked good work comes back in line. Inspect first, then block only what's wrong.

timeout.speaker: agent
timeout.text: I waited so long, I rounded the clock. It says 2 PM now.

winWithMisses.speaker: agent
winWithMisses.text: Practice done! Some of my plans went out. A few charts on the wall point down.

winWithMisses.speaker: coach
winWithMisses.text: That's what practice is for. Look first, then decide. The real shift is next.

debrief.takeaway: Inspect first. Then ask: Who signed off? What was asked? Can we undo it? Block only what the evidence says is wrong.
debrief.careerInsight: Analysts check each other's reports before they go out. They check the source, the sign-off and who can see it. AI agents draft reports fast, so the human check matters more.
